title: A Little Bit of Everything
description: Five stops through places, stories, music, history and science.

questions.question: What is the capital of Portugal?
questions.explanation: Lisbon is Portugal’s capital, on the country’s Atlantic coast.

questions.question: In which classic film does Dorothy follow the Yellow Brick Road?
questions.explanation: Dorothy travels toward the Emerald City in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz.

questions.question: Which band recorded the album Abbey Road?
questions.explanation: Abbey Road was released by the Beatles in 1969.

questions.question: Which English king agreed to the Magna Carta in 1215?
questions.explanation: King John sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede in June 1215.

questions.question: Which element has the chemical symbol W?
questions.explanation: W is tungsten’s symbol, derived from its older name, wolfram.

title: Culture, Sport & Surprises
description: A quick tour from the tennis court to art, brands and numbers.

questions.question: What playing surface is used for the main courts at Wimbledon?
questions.explanation: The Championships at Wimbledon are played on grass courts.

questions.question: Who painted the work commonly known as Girl with a Pearl Earring?
questions.explanation: The Dutch painter Johannes Vermeer created the work around 1665.

questions.question: The LEGO Group began in which country?
questions.explanation: The LEGO Group was founded in Billund, Denmark.

questions.question: Nelson Mandela was born in which present-day country?
questions.explanation: Mandela was born in Mvezo, in what is now South Africa.

questions.question: What is the smallest prime number greater than 50?
questions.explanation: 51 and 57 are divisible by 3, while 53 is prime.

title: Around the World
description: Use rivers, coastlines and landmarks to find your way across the map.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal stands in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal is in Agra, in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which river flows through Budapest?
questions.explanation: The Danube runs through Budapest, separating the historic areas of Buda and Pest.

questions.question: Reykjavík is the capital of which island country?
questions.explanation: Reykjavík is Iceland’s capital and largest city.

questions.question: The Bosporus connects the Black Sea to which smaller sea?
questions.explanation: The Bosporus runs between the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara in Türkiye.

questions.question: Which country has coastlines on both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.explanation: Iran borders the Caspian Sea to the north and the Persian Gulf to the south.

title: Big Screen, Big Ideas
description: A blend of film, music, history, science and geography.

questions.question: Kyoto is a city in which country?
questions.explanation: Kyoto is a historic city on Japan’s main island of Honshu.

questions.question: Who directed the 1975 film Jaws?
questions.explanation: Steven Spielberg directed Jaws, adapted from Peter Benchley’s novel.

questions.question: Which instrument is Yo-Yo Ma best known for playing?
questions.explanation: Yo-Yo Ma is a renowned cellist who performs classical and other musical styles.

questions.question: Which Norman duke won the Battle of Hastings in 1066?
questions.explanation: William, Duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold II and later became king of England.

questions.question: At about 25°C, what pH value is neutral in pure water?
questions.explanation: At approximately 25°C, pure water is neutral at pH 7.

title: A World of Stories
description: From France’s roads to a novel, a brand and some brain-teasing facts.

questions.question: The Tour de France is an annual professional race in which sport?
questions.explanation: The Tour de France is a multi-stage road cycling race held primarily in France.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Frankenstein?
questions.explanation: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein, first published anonymously in 1818.

questions.question: IKEA was founded in which country?
questions.explanation: Ingvar Kamprad founded IKEA in Älmhult, Sweden, in 1943.

questions.question: Florence Nightingale became known for her nursing work during which war?
questions.explanation: Nightingale and her team cared for British soldiers during the Crimean War.

questions.question: Which mathematical constant is approximately 2.71828?
questions.explanation: The constant e, the base of natural logarithms, is approximately 2.71828.

title: Ideas That Changed the World
description: Five milestones in the history of inventions and technology.

questions.question: Which inventor is associated with the movable-type printing press in 15th-century Europe?
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg developed a practical movable-type printing system in Mainz.

questions.question: Who proposed the World Wide Web while working at CERN?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989.

questions.question: Which Scottish engineer made major improvements to the steam engine in the 18th century?
questions.explanation: James Watt’s improvements made steam engines substantially more efficient.

questions.question: In 1903, the Wright brothers achieved the first what in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina?
answers: Crossing of the Atlantic by air
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered aircraft in 1903.

questions.question: Which American inventor sent the famous message “What hath God wrought” by telegraph in 1844?
questions.explanation: Samuel Morse sent the message from Washington, D.C., to Baltimore in a public demonstration of the telegraph.

title: Curiosity, Connected
description: Five fresh questions across the map, the arts, sport, music and science.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Greece and Türkiye?
questions.explanation: The Aegean Sea lies between the Greek mainland and the western coast of Türkiye.

questions.question: How many interlaced rings are on the Olympic symbol?
questions.explanation: The Olympic symbol has five interlaced rings.

questions.question: Who composed the violin concertos known as The Four Seasons?
questions.explanation: Antonio Vivaldi published The Four Seasons as part of his collection Il cimento dell’armonia e dell’inventione.

questions.question: The ancient city of Carthage stood near the site of which modern capital?
questions.explanation: Carthage’s archaeological site lies near Tunis, the capital of Tunisia.

questions.question: Which SI base unit measures luminous intensity?
questions.explanation: The candela is the SI base unit for luminous intensity; lumen and lux are derived units.
